newsitem.title: UK: Zeneca breaks 1 billion stg profit barrier.
newsitem.headline: Zeneca breaks 1 billion stg profit barrier.

text.p: Britain's third-largest drugs company Zeneca Group Plc broke through the billion-pound pre-tax profit barrier on Tuesday, propelled by strong growth in pharmaceuticals and agricultural chemicals.

The bioscience group said 1996 pre-tax profit before exceptional charges soared to 1.011 billion pounds ($1.6 billion) a year before, above the top end of analysts' forecasts. ($ = 0.624 British Pounds)

The company's 13 percent rise in drug sales to 2.44 billion pounds dwarfed the six percent rise reported by Glaxo Wellcome Plc last week. Operating profit on pharmaceutical sales rose 10 percent to 757 million pounds from 687 million.

Growth was driven by sales of cardiovascular drug Zestril, which rose 10 percent despite increased competition. Sales of established prostate cancer drug Zoladex rose 31 percent and newly-launched prostate cancer drug Casodex "exceeded expectations" with sales of 68 million pounds.
The company also announced the approval of its new migraine drug Zomig, acquired from Glaxo Wellcome Plc, in the UK on Monday.

Looking ahead Zeneca said it expected further "strong volume growth" in 1997, but warned that market development and launch costs for new drugs and chemicals "will continue to restrain short-term profit growth, but should significantly enhance the long-term prospects of the group." --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
